title: Nine Falsifiable Predictions About Artificial Intelligence and Global Health: A Grounded Forecasting Framework from the Global South (2025–2075)
content: Background: AI is deployed across global health systems with growing reach, yet rigorous long-range forecasting about its equity implications — particularly from Global South institutional vantage points — remains sparse. Most AI-in-health literature either describes current deployment states or projects forward over short horizons of five to ten years. Publicly committed, falsifiable predictions over decadal and multi-decadal timescales are almost entirely absent.Methods: Nine falsifiable predictions about AI and global health for 2025–2075 are developed through three analytical components applied to each prediction: systematic review of current peer-reviewed evidence trajectories; historical analogy analysis drawing on comparable technological transitions in global health; and governance trajectory analysis examining international health law, African Union policy frameworks, WHO guidance, and published AI governance literature. Each prediction carries an explicit confidence classification — High, Medium, or Conditional — alongside a named counterfactual and a defined verification horizon.Findings: The predictions address: AI-assisted diagnostic equity by 2040; augmentation of community health worker roles by 2035; the emergence and predictable insufficiency of a Global AI Equity Treaty by 2035; administrative AI displacement in high-burden health systems by 2045; African frugal AI health innovation leadership in the 2040s; climate-health AI as the dominant outbreak detection system by 2050; federated learning as a partial data sovereignty solution; pandemic AI preventing a COVID-equivalent while governance gaps persist; and the 2075 global health system materially improving, contingent on governance decisions made before 2045.Interpretation: The determining variable across all nine predictions is governance architecture, not technological capability. The Anaweokhai Protocols — a five-domain governance framework for AI health data in the Global South — are introduced as a structural response to the governance deficits identified.
